description: Arabizi -> Arabic phoneme tables for arabizikit. Digraphs are tried longest-first before single letters. 'alternatives' lists are in priority order and are used to generate ranked candidate transliterations. v0.3 adds the Maghrebi conventions: ch reads as shin (French-influenced spelling, tch for the rare tsh reading), 9 reads as qaf in Morocco (sad in Egypt, dad as 9'), and 8 reads as ghayn or heh depending on the writer.

2.note: The most ambiguous Arabizi character: glottal stop / hamza in Egypt and the Levant, qaf in Gulf and Iraq. Context rules and the lexicon resolve the common cases.

8.note: 8 is qaf in the Egyptian convention, ghayn in the Gulf, and heh in some Moroccan writing (n8ar -> نهار). 8' is ghayn.

9.note: 9 is sad in the Egyptian convention (9ba7 -> صباح), qaf in Moroccan Darija (yb9aw -> يبقاو), and dad as 9' (ra9'e -> راضي). A dialect hint (transliterate(..., dialect_hint=...)) picks the regional reading; without one, sad stays the global default.

a.note: a is usually long alif, but a short a is often elided (3alayk -> عليك via the alternative); the ain reading is a distant alternative.

e.note: Shwa / short e is usually elided in writing (3emel -> عمل).

g.note: Egyptian g = ج; Gulf g is often ق (gamar).

i.note: Medial i between consonants is often a short vowel (bint -> بنت via the alternative).

o.note: Short o is often elided (2akol -> آكل via the alternative).

u.note: Short u is often elided (shukran -> شكرا via the alternative).

T.note: The Moroccan convention uses capitals for emphatic readings: T for ta (Tab3an -> طبعا), S for sad (9Sdti -> قصدتي).

context_rules.note: sou2 -> سوق, tare2 -> طريق, fo2 -> فوق
2alb -> قلب (Gulf qaf) vs 2ktob -> اكتب (imperative alif). Both are produced as ranked candidates.
7elwa -> حلوة (taa marbuta) is the default; hada -> هذا (alif) is the alternative, and the lexicon overrides the top ambiguous words. Ya (ى) covers the Maghrebi -a/-aa spelling (b9a -> بقى).
